answer: Seven established neighbors form a prism around each claim, each checking a facet. A pulse each epoch demands fresh attestations; none signs more than three. Each signature costs 10, so one identity pays 70. The quorum grows with the tide of registrations, plus one per 10,000. 1,000 fakes need 7,000 signatures: 70,000 against a 40,000 pool, a 30,000 loss. An honest agent pays 70 once, keeps its share; a rented-neighbor ring fails on the cap.
